fair_value_reason: P/E: 18.5-19x NTM EPS of ~$4.55-4.65 at Sep-2027 (575M shares, ~8% tax, light haircut to consensus) = ~$86. FCF yield (equity basis, FCF after interest and before the ~$111M preferred dividend, over 575M as-converted shares): ~$2.45-2.6B FY28 FCF at a 5.0-5.2% required yield = $85.2-87.0 (2.45/0.05/0.575; 2.6/0.052/0.575), no net-debt deduction because FCF is already after interest. EV/EBITDA: harmonized at ~16x on ~$3.2B EBITDA, less $3.8B net debt, = ~$82, instead of the agents' 14-15x ($73-78), which double-counts the derating already in the P/E multiple. Weighted about 0.5/0.3/0.2, that gives ~$85, slightly above the $84.3 forecaster mean.

thesis_triggers.event: $55 is ~12x FY28 consensus EPS ($4.58) and ~30% below spot. A close there would mean the market is pricing an outright cycle reversal: book-to-bill below 1, GM guided back toward ~60-62%, and distributor inventory rebuilding from 25 days. Below ~$62.5 the mandatory convertible also delivers more shares (up to ~29M below ~$51), adding dilution into weakness.

supervisor_summary: After round 1's fact corrections the five forecasts converged tightly: fair values $83-86, ladder medians ~$83-85, all using $4.58 FY28 consensus, ~7.5-8% tax, 575M shares and ~$3.8B Sep-2027 net debt. New searches found nothing that changes the fundamentals. The latest news is a product launch, the Hailo close and a 10-yr UST at 5.14%, so I keep the forecasters' mean ladder (P(>= $79) ~0.56, median ~$84) and put fair value at $85, ~8% above spot plus a ~2.3% dividend. The main risk is an upcycle that peaks around mid-2027, just before the horizon, together with high rates capping semis multiples. The next checkpoint is Q2 FY27 results around early November.
key_drivers: FY28 (Mar-2028) consensus EPS is $4.58 on $7.43B revenue (S&P Global consensus via StockAnalysis, data as of 2026-09-18). At the 2026-09-25 close of $78.69 the stock trades at ~17.2x FY28 consensus and ~19.1x NTM (estimate: half FY27 $3.65 + half FY28 $4.58 = $4.12).

Gross margin is guided flat at 66-67% into the December quarter (through-cycle model 65%). The full-quarter effect of the Aug/Sep price increase replaces the one-time September-quarter licensing and repricing gains.

The channel is lean: distributor inventory is 25 days, at the low end of its historical range (CFO, Q1 FY27 call), and management sees no significant customer stocking or inventory build (Citi TMT, 2026-09-09). Cycle risk sits in mid-2027, near the horizon, when the market prices FY29.

Deleveraging is slow: net debt was $5.09B in Jun-2026 and falls ~$250-300M a quarter (estimate; the June quarter was ~$170M) after ~$1.1B a year of common and preferred dividends, reaching ~$3.8B by Sep-2027 (5.09 - 5 x ~0.26). There are no buybacks until then.

Rates and sector multiple: the 10-yr UST is ~5.1-5.2% (5.17% Treasury close on 2026-09-25) and semis derated after the July-2026 selloff, which caps MCHP near 18.5-19x NTM. The next test is Q2 FY27 results, expected ~2026-11-05 (not yet confirmed).
